claims.text: metrics-server collects Pods' current CPU and memory use from the kubelets and serves it through the API server via an APIService registered for metrics.k8s.io (kubectl get apiservice v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io), for kubectl top and autoscaling; short-term, in memory, no history.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Resource metrics pipeline (Metrics API: register an APIService for metrics.k8s.io); Tools for monitoring resources

claims.text: An HPA's control loop (in the control plane) repeatedly sets the scale target's replica count within minReplicas and maxReplicas from observed metrics such as CPU; at maxReplicas it still computes and shows the metric, only the count is capped (ScalingLimited).
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Horizontal Pod Autoscaling > How does a HorizontalPodAutoscaler work?; HPA walkthrough > conditions (ScalingLimited)

claims.text: For a CPU Utilization target, the HPA computes each Pod's use as a percentage of its CPU request and averages it; desiredReplicas = ceil(currentReplicas × current / desired), kept within min and max; no action when the ratio is within the tolerance of 1.0.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Horizontal Pod Autoscaling > Algorithm details

claims.text: Worked arithmetic: request 50m, target 50%: use 100m = 200% gives ceil(1 × 200/50) = 4; use 75m = 150% gives 3; both within maxReplicas 5.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Horizontal Pod Autoscaling > Algorithm details; cpu-echo.yaml and cpu-echo-hpa.yaml @ stage-4

claims.text: The HPA updates the target Deployment's replica count, and the Deployment's ReplicaSet creates or removes Pods accordingly.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Horizontal Pod Autoscaling (scale subresource); Deployments > Scaling a Deployment

claims.text: If a Pod's containers set no CPU request, CPU utilization is undefined and the HPA takes no action for that metric; with no metrics available (as on donhang), kubectl get hpa shows the target as <unknown> and the count stays unchanged.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Horizontal Pod Autoscaling > Algorithm details (missing metrics, resource requests); Support for resource metrics

claims.text: Scale-down uses a stabilization window (behavior.scaleDown.stabilizationWindowSeconds) before lowering the count; its default is 300 seconds; cpu-echo-hpa.yaml sets 30.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Horizontal Pod Autoscaling > Configurable scaling behavior > Stabilization window / Default Behavior

claims.text: cpu-echo-hpa.yaml @ stage-4: autoscaling/v2 HPA cpu-echo in autoscale-lessons, scaleTargetRef Deployment cpu-echo, min 1, max 5, cpu Utilization 50, scaleDown window 30; comment lines 1-5 say the Deployment sets no replicas and the default is 300 s.

cpu-echo.yaml @ stage-4 (not shown): namespace autoscale-lessons; Caddy answering every request, so CPU use grows with requests (comment lines 1-4); container echo requests cpu 50m; Deployment sets no replicas.

With Argo CD, a Deployment that keeps spec.replicas in Git is set back to that value when the HPA changes it (at once with self-heal, otherwise at the next sync); the recommended approach is to leave replicas out of the manifest.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Automated Sync Policy > Automatic Self-Healing; Diffing Customization / best practices on replicas with HPA; devops.l3.self-heal

claims.text: autoscale.sh @ stage-4: creates donhang if absent; waits up to 180 s each for rollout, ScalingActive, load Pod, then 60 s load. Output: Metrics API not available; apiservice NotFound; cpu: <unknown>/50%, 1 replica; AbleToScale=True, ScalingActive=False (FailedGetResourceMetric); Deployment 1/1.
claims.source_hint: outputs/stage-4/scripts/k8s/autoscale.txt; scripts/k8s/autoscale.sh lines 7-54; scripts/lib/network-lessons.sh lessons_cluster; HPA walkthrough (AbleToScale, ScalingActive meaning)

claims.text: The HPA's CPU utilization target is computed against requests, not limits; the container limit plays no part in the calculation.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Horizontal Pod Autoscaling > Algorithm details (percentage of the equivalent resource request)

claims.text: A ResourceQuota on a namespace counts the requests of every Pod created in it, including Pods added by an HPA.

Opinion: with steady load and headroom, keep fixed replicas in Git; when a load test shows api is CPU-bound at a peak, use an HPA on CPU with min for quiet load and max within what nodes and the database carry.
Opinion: when the bottleneck is the database or a shared limit while api CPU stays low, an HPA on CPU does not see it and more api Pods only queue requests at the same place.
claims.source_hint: trade-off reasoning; backend.l4.load-testing (Little's law, waiting at a full shared resource)
